description.narrative:
Goal: The program goal is to accelerate the adoption of clean cooking solutions by the poor and underserved populations in Tanzania. This goal will be achieved through the following objectives:
Objectives: i. Catalyze the private sector participation in clean cooking solutions in poor population and underserved markets ii. Accelerate the uptake of clean cooking solutions through innovative financing mechanisms and technical assistance to selected private sector companies iii. Strengthen the clean cooking sector coordination and advocate for a conducive policy environment for a market led clean cooking sector.
Focus areas : Rural and marginalized communities in urban, peri-urban and rural areas
Target primary beneficiaries: • Poor people • Early and growth stage private sector enterprises through grant funding, business assistance and technical assistance • Business Member Organization including TAREA

Tanzania Clean Cooking Project (TCCP) är ett treårigt program som syftar till att förvandla den rena matlagningssektorn genom ökat deltagande från den privata sektorn. Programmet syftar till att ta itu med den dubbla utmaningen med utbud och efterfrågan genom innovativa mekanismer som förringar investeringar från den privata sektorn (utbudssidan) och gör rena matlagningslösningar mer överkomliga (efterfrågesidan).

The Tanzania Clean Cooking Project (TCCP) is a three-year program that aims to transform the clean cooking sector through enhanced private sector participation. The program aims to address the two-fold challenge of supply and demand through innovative mechanisms that derisk private sector investments (supply side) and make clean cooking solutions more affordable (demand side).

The Annual Narrative Report presents the progress made in the implementation of project activities during the 2024/25 financial year, highlighting key achievements, impacts realized, challenges encountered, and lessons learned. By the end of the reporting period, AECF had contracted nine (9) companies, while two additional companies had been approved by the Investment Committee (IC) and were expected to be contracted in October or November 2025.
According to the latest update received from AECF on 13 July 2026, the project has since expanded its portfolio, with a total of thirteen (13) companies now contracted and actively implementing clean cooking business initiatives with support from the Tanzania Clean Cooking Project (TCCP). This represents continued progress in scaling up private sector participation and advancing the adoption of clean cooking solutions across Tanzania.
The supported companies represent a diverse portfolio of clean cooking solutions, including improved household cooking stoves, large institutional stoves, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), and briquette manufacturing. During the reporting period, the companies received technical assistance in areas such as business formalisation, accounting procedures, marketing strategies, and reporting practices.
The cumulative implementation results of the Tanzania Clean Cooking Project (TCCP) demonstrate strong overall performance, with the project meeting or exceeding most of its key performance indicators by the end of the 2025/2026 reporting period. The achievements reflect the effectiveness of the project's market based approach in expanding access to clean cooking solutions and strengthening private sector participation.
The project significantly surpassed its target for households accessing clean cooking solutions. Against a target of 90,000 households, the project reached a cumulative total of 188,438 households, representing 209% achievement. This exceptional performance indicates a rapid uptake of clean cooking technologies and successful outreach by the supported companies. During the 2024/2025 financial year, 119,496 households were reached, followed by an additional 68,942 households in 2025/2026.
The project also achieved its target for private sector companies supported. A total of 13 companies were contracted and operational against a target range of 1315 companies, resulting in 100% achievement of the minimum target. The expansion of the portfolio demonstrates the project's success in attracting and supporting private sector investment in Tanzania's clean cooking market.
In terms of lives impacted, the project reached 942,190 people, more than double the household beneficiaries and significantly exceeding the target of 450,000 lives, achieving 152% of the planned target. This reflects the broader social benefits of increased household access to clean cooking technologies, including improved health, environmental, and economic outcomes.
The project also performed well in mobilizing private sector matching funds. Against a target of USD 1.5 million, the supported companies mobilized approximately USD 1.73 million, representing 115% achievement. This demonstrates strong private sector commitment and confidence in the clean cooking market, while reducing reliance on donor funding.
Employment creation also exceeded expectations. The project created a cumulative 245 jobs compared to the target of 225 jobs, achieving 108% of the target. This indicates that the project has contributed not only to clean energy access but also to local economic development and job creation. Similarly, the project surpassed its target for institutional stoves sold. A total of 678 institutional stoves were sold against a target of 400, achieving approximately 170% of the target. This suggests growing demand for clean cooking solutions among institutions such as schools, hospitals, and other public facilities.
Support to small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) also exceeded expectations. The project supported 974 SMEs, compared to the target of 774, representing 126% achievement. This demonstrates the project's contribution to strengthening local entrepreneurship and expanding market distribution networks for clean cooking technologies.
The only indicator that remains below target is CO2 emissions avoided. By the end of the reporting period, the project had avoided 110,868 tonnes of CO against a target of 350,000 tonnes, representing 31% achievement. While household adoption and market expansion have been highly successful, the environmental benefits measured through carbon emissions reductions have not yet materialized at the anticipated level. This may reflect the time required for sustained use of clean cooking technologies, differences in technology types and fuel displacement, or conservative methodologies for estimating emissions reductions. Continued monitoring and longer term use of the technologies are expected to increase cumulative CO reductions over time.
Overall, the project's performance demonstrates substantial progress and strong value for investment. Most indicators have exceeded their targets, highlighting the effectiveness of the project's implementation strategy, successful engagement with the private sector, and increasing adoption of clean cooking solutions across Tanzania. Going forward, particular attention should be given to enhancing the measurement and realization of carbon emission reductions while sustaining the momentum achieved in market expansion, household adoption, and private sector investment.
